explain.say: In November 1884 diplomats from fourteen states met in Berlin to agree rules for claiming Africa. Not one African was invited. Historians stress that the conference did not draw the map itself; it set rules like effective occupation, which sped up the grab. Look at the timeline of conquest and resistance.

explain.say: See the sizes. Around 1870 European states ruled roughly a tenth of Africa, mostly coasts. By 1914 they ruled about nine tenths. Only Ethiopia and Liberia stayed independent. That is one of the fastest land grabs in history. What would you need to conquer so much land so quickly?

Here are the reasons. Rivalry between powers, hopes of rubber, gold and markets, and racist ideas of a civilising mission. Technology made it possible: quinine against malaria, steamships up rivers, and the Maxim machine gun. At Omdurman in Sudan in 1898 about 10,000 Sudanese soldiers died, against under fifty on the British side. Which reason surprises you?

draw.question: Why did Europe carve up Africa so fast?

because.label: Rivalry
because.note: Prestige; new powers Germany and Italy.

because.label: Local crises
because.note: Egypt 1882 set off a chain of claims.

draw.answer: Rivalry and profit, made possible by new weapons.

explain.say: Africans resisted. On 1 March 1896 at Adwa, Emperor Menelik the Second's Ethiopian army defeated Italy, keeping Ethiopia free. In Leopold the Second's Congo, forced rubber labour brought mutilation and mass death; in Namibia, German forces killed most of the Herero and many Nama, a genocide Germany acknowledged in 2021. We remember the victims. See the map.

Now the debate. John Hobson and Lenin saw capitalists seeking profit; Ronald Robinson and John Gallagher saw officials guarding routes to India, set off by the Egypt crisis, with African politics shaping events. Careful work today. Exam tip: use one case, like Egypt or Congo, to test each theory.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Profit, strategy and African politics mixed.

faq.q: What was the Scramble for Africa?
faq.a: The rapid conquest and division of Africa by European powers between about 1880 and 1914. European rule grew from roughly 10 percent of the continent to about 90 percent, leaving only Ethiopia and Liberia independent.
asks: How much of Africa did Europe rule by 1914?

faq.q: Did the Berlin Conference divide Africa?
faq.a: Not directly. The 1884 to 1885 conference set rules, such as notifying others and showing effective occupation, and recognised Leopold II's Congo Free State. The actual borders were drawn in many later treaties and conquests.
asks: What was decided at the Berlin Conference?

faq.a: Emperor Menelik II built a large army with modern rifles and defeated the Italian invasion at Adwa on 1 March 1896. Italy recognised Ethiopian independence, until it invaded again in 1935.
asks: What happened at the Battle of Adwa?

faq.q: What happened in the Congo Free State?
faq.a: From 1885 King Leopold II of Belgium ruled the Congo as his own colony. Forced labour to collect rubber, hostage-taking and mutilation caused mass deaths; estimates vary widely. International outrage led Belgium to take it over in 1908.

faq.q: What was the Herero and Nama genocide?
faq.a: Between 1904 and 1908 German colonial forces in present-day Namibia killed most of the Herero people and about half of the Nama, through killings, starvation in the desert and camps. Germany officially acknowledged it as genocide in 2021.
asks: What did Germany do in Namibia?

facts: The Berlin Conference met from November 1884 to February 1885.
Ethiopia defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa on 1 March 1896.
By 1914 only Ethiopia and Liberia in Africa were independent of European rule.

quiz.say: By 1914, about what share of Africa was under European rule?
quiz.why: European control grew from about a tenth in 1870 to about nine tenths by 1914.

wrong.1: About 10 percent was the share around 1870.
wrong.2: By 1914 the share was far higher than half.

quiz.say: Which African state defeated a European army at Adwa in 1896?
quiz.show: At Adwa, Italy was defeated by…
quiz.why: Menelik II's Ethiopian army beat Italy and kept Ethiopia independent.

wrong.1: Liberia stayed independent but did not fight at Adwa.
wrong.2: Egypt was under British occupation from 1882.
